title: Wacky Cake: The Depression-Era Cake With No Eggs or Milk
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Have an 8-inch square or 9-inch round baking pan ready (greasing is optional if mixing directly in the pan, but makes serving easier).
Sift the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt directly into the pan and stir together with a fork until evenly combined.
Use a spoon to make three wells in the dry mixture. Pour the oil into one well, the vinegar into the second, and the vanilla into the third.
Pour the cold water evenly over everything.
Stir with a fork just until no streaks of dry flour remain and the batter is smooth; a few small lumps are fine, do not overmix.
Bake 30-35 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before dusting with powdered sugar or topping with a simple glaze.

title: Depression-Era Vanilla Cake: The Original Crazy Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Have an 8-inch square or 9-inch round baking pan ready.
Sift the flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt directly into the pan and stir together with a fork until evenly combined.
Make three wells in the dry mixture. Pour the oil into one, the vinegar into the second, and the vanilla and almond extract into the third.
Pour the cold water evenly over everything.
Stir with a fork just until the batter is smooth and no dry flour remains; do not overmix.
Bake 28-32 minutes, checking a few minutes early, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with just a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before glazing, frosting, or serving plain.

title: Depression-Era Tomato Soup Cake: An Old Pantry Trick
ingredients: 1 can (10.75 oz) condensed tomato soup, undiluted
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a 9x13-inch pan or two 9-inch round cake pans.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg.
In a large bowl, cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in the egg.
Beat in the tomato soup until smooth (the mixture may look slightly curdled — that's normal).
Gradually add the dry ingredients, mixing just until combined.
Fold in the raisins and walnuts, if using.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake 30-35 minutes (25-30 minutes for round pans), until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely before frosting with cream cheese frosting or a simple sugar glaze.

title: Vinegar Pie: The Depression Dessert That Tastes Like Lemon
ingredients: 1/2 cup water (or milk for a richer pie)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edges.
In a bowl, whisk together the sugar, flour, and salt.
Add the eggs and whisk until smooth.
Whisk in the vinegar, water, melted butter, and vanilla until fully combined.
Pour the filling into the prepared crust.
Bake 40-45 minutes, until the center is just set and no longer jiggles and the top is golden.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then chill at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Depression-Era Banana Bread from Overripe Bananas
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Cream the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the egg.
Mix in the mashed bananas and vanilla.
Add the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; fold in the nuts, if using.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan.
Bake 55-65 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing.

title: Depression-Era Bread and Butter Pickles Recipe
steps: Combine the cucumbers and onion in a large bowl, sprinkle with the salt, and toss to coat. Cover with ice and let stand 2-3 hours, then drain and rinse well.
In a large pot, combine the vinegar, sugar, mustard seed, celery seed, turmeric, and cloves. Bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the drained cucumbers and onion to the brine and return to a simmer for 2-3 minutes, until just heated through.
For refrigerator pickles: ladle into clean jars, cool, and refrigerate; ready to eat within 24 hours and keeps for several weeks.
For shelf-stable pickles: pack the hot pickles and brine into sterilized jars leaving 1/2-inch headspace, wipe the rims, seal with lids, and process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes.
Let processed jars cool completely and confirm the lids have sealed before storing in a cool, dark place.

title: Water Pie: A Great Depression Dessert From Almost Nothing
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edges.
In a saucepan, whisk together the sugar and flour, then whisk in the water until smooth.
Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the butter, vanilla, and salt until the butter melts.
Pour the hot filling into the prepared crust and sprinkle with a little cinnamon.
Bake 35-40 minutes, until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbling and starting to set.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate at least 3-4 hours to let the filling fully set before slicing.

title: Hoover Stew: The Great Depression's Resourceful One-Pot Meal
ingredients: 1 pound hot dogs, sliced into rounds
1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the sliced hot dogs and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, both cans of beans, macaroni, water, and garlic powder.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes, until the macaroni is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
If the stew is too thick, stir in a little more water; let it rest a few minutes before serving.

title: Poor Man's Meal: Fried Potatoes, Onions and Hot Dogs
ingredients: 4 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
3 tablespoons bacon grease, butter, or vegetable oil
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the fat in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes, season with salt and pepper, cover, and cook 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until nearly tender.
Add the onion and continue cooking uncovered for 5 minutes.
Add the sliced hot dogs and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are golden and crisp at the edges and the hot dogs are browned, 8-10 minutes more.
Season with additional salt, pepper, and paprika if using.
Serve hot straight from the skillet.

title: Depression-Era Oatmeal Cookies: Thrifty 1930s Drop Cookies
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter or shortening, softened
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Cream the butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla and molasses.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, mixing until just combined.
Stir in the oats and raisins by hand.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared baking sheets, spacing 2 inches apart.
Bake 10-12 minutes, until the edges are golden but the centers still look slightly soft.
Cool on the baking sheet 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

title: Mock Apple Pie: The Depression-Era Dessert With No Apples
ingredients: 36 buttery round crackers (such as Ritz), coarsely broken
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Fit the bottom crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
In a saucepan, combine the water, sugar, and cream of tartar; bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then simmer 10 minutes to form a syrup. Cool slightly.
Stir the lemon juice and zest into the syrup.
Scatter the broken crackers evenly into the bottom crust.
Pour the warm syrup evenly over the crackers and let stand a few minutes to soften.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and dot with the butter.
Cover with the top crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut several slits for steam to escape.
Bake 15 minutes at 425°F, then reduce heat to 350°F and bake another 30-35 minutes, until the crust is golden brown.
Cool at least 2 hours before slicing to let the filling set.

title: Peanut Butter Bread: A Thrifty Depression-Era Quick Bread
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the peanut butter into the milk until mostly smooth (small lumps are fine); whisk in the honey if using.
Pour the peanut butter mixture into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; do not overmix.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake 50-55 minutes, until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing.

title: Old-Fashioned American Goulash: A Depression-Era Comfort Meal
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: In a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef with the onion, breaking up the meat, until the beef is cooked through; drain excess fat.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, water, Worcestershire sauce, Italian seasoning, and sugar.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 10 minutes to blend the flavors.
Stir in the uncooked macaroni, cover, and simmer 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Top with shredded cheddar if desired and serve hot.

title: Creamed Chipped Beef on Toast: The Classic SOS Breakfast
ingredients: 1 jar (2.25-2.5 oz) dried beef, torn into small pieces
1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or more to taste
Salt, to taste (optional, beef is salty)
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in the milk, a little at a time, until smooth.
Cook, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and just comes to a simmer, about 5-6 minutes.
Stir in the torn dried beef and black pepper; simmer 2-3 minutes, until the beef is heated through.
Taste and add salt only if needed.
Spoon the creamed beef generously over the toast and serve immediately.

title: Old-Fashioned Navy Bean Soup with a Leftover Ham Bone
ingredients: 1 lb dried navy beans, rinsed and picked over
1 meaty ham bone (or 2 cups diced cooked ham plus 1 smoked ham hock)
1 tablespoon butter or bacon drippings (optional, for sauteing)
steps: Place the dried navy beans in a large bowl, cover with several inches of cold water, and soak overnight (or quick-soak: boil 2 minutes, then let stand 1 hour). Drain and rinse.
In a large stockpot or Dutch oven, melt the butter or bacon drippings over medium heat and saute the onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Add the soaked beans, ham bone, water or broth, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover partially, and simmer 2 to 2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans are tender and the broth has thickened.
Remove the ham bone, pull off any meat, dice it, and return the meat to the pot; discard the bone and bay leaves.
For a creamier soup, mash a cupful of beans against the side of the pot and stir back in.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and simmer 10 more minutes before serving hot.

title: Old-Fashioned Johnny Cakes (Cornmeal Griddle Cakes)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons bacon drippings or butter, melted, plus more for the griddle
steps: In a heatproof bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, salt, and sugar.
Pour the boiling water over the cornmeal, stirring constantly, until a thick mush forms; let stand 5 minutes.
Stir in the milk (start with 1/2 cup and add more for a thinner batter), the egg if using, and the melted fat until smooth.
Heat a griddle or heavy skillet over medium heat and grease lightly with bacon drippings.
Drop the batter by scant 1/4-cupfuls onto the hot griddle, spreading slightly with the back of a spoon.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp at the edges, flipping once.
Serve hot with butter and molasses or syrup.

title: Old-Fashioned Creamy Potato Soup, Simple and Hearty
ingredients: 6 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
1 1/2 cups whole milk or 1 (12 oz) can evaporated milk
2 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled (optional, for garnish)
Chopped chives or parsley, for garnish
steps: In a large pot, melt the bacon drippings over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and water or broth; bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash about half the potatoes right in the pot with a potato masher for a creamy texture, leaving the rest in chunks.
In a small bowl, whisk the flour into 1/4 cup of the milk until smooth, then stir this into the pot along with the remaining milk.
Simmer gently over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thickened; do not let it boil hard.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls and top with crumbled bacon and chives before serving.

title: Old-Fashioned Spiced Prune Cake, Moist and Nostalgic
ingredients: 1/2 cup vegetable oil or melted butter
steps: Preheat the oven to 350F. Grease and flour a 9-inch square or round cake pan, or a bundt pan.
Cover the prunes with 1/2 cup of the buttermilk and simmer gently in a small saucepan for 5 minutes, or microwave to soften; cool slightly, then chop finely.
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.
In a large bowl, beat the sugar and oil or butter together, then beat in the eggs one at a time and the vanilla.
Add the flour mixture alternately with the remaining 1/2 cup buttermilk, beginning and ending with the flour, mixing just until combined.
Fold in the chopped prunes and nuts if using.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake 35 to 40 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely before slicing.

title: Old-Fashioned Salmon Patties From Canned Salmon
ingredients: 1 (14.75 oz) can salmon, drained, skin and large bones removed
1/3 cup breadcrumbs or crushed saltine crackers
3 tablespoons bacon drippings or vegetable oil, for frying
steps: In a mixing bowl, flake the drained salmon well with a fork, checking for any remaining bones.
Add the beaten egg, breadcrumbs, chopped onion, mayonnaise if using, lemon juice, pepper, and salt.
Mix gently until just combined, then shape into 6 to 8 patties about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat the bacon drippings in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Fry the patties in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden brown and firm all the way through.
Drain briefly on paper towels.
Serve hot, with a simple white sauce, tartar sauce, or a squeeze of lemon.

title: Old-Fashioned Corn Fritters, Crispy and Golden
ingredients: 2 cups fresh, frozen (thawed), or well-drained canned corn kernels
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs and milk together, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the corn kernels until evenly distributed; the batter should be thick enough to hold its shape when dropped from a spoon.
Heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat.
Drop the batter by heaping tablespoonfuls into the hot oil, flattening slightly, and fry in batches without crowding the pan.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, plain or with syrup.

title: Old-Fashioned Soft Spiced Molasses Cookies Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup granulated sugar, plus extra for rolling
steps: In a large bowl, cream the shortening and 1 cup sugar together until light and fluffy.
Beat in the molasses and egg until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves.
Stir the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until a soft dough forms.
Cover and chill the dough at least 1 hour, or until firm enough to handle.
Preheat the oven to 350F and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls, then roll each ball in the extra sugar and place 2 inches apart on the prepared sheets.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the tops crack but the centers still look slightly underdone.
Let cool on the sheet for 2 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

title: Hoosier Sugar Cream Pie, Indiana's Classic Dessert
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
steps: Preheat the oven to 375F. Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edges.
In a bowl, whisk together the sugar, flour, and salt.
Whisk in the cream, milk, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the filling into the unbaked crust.
Dot the top evenly with the butter pieces and sprinkle generously with nutmeg.
Bake 40 to 50 minutes, until the edges are set and golden and the center still jiggles slightly.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Old-Fashioned Southern Chocolate Gravy and Biscuits
steps: In a saucepan, whisk together the sugar, cocoa powder, flour, and salt until no lumps remain.
Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth.
Place over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture comes to a gentle boil and thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the butter and vanilla until melted and glossy.
If the gravy is too thick, whisk in a splash more warm milk; if too thin, return to low heat for another minute.
Split warm biscuits and ladle the hot chocolate gravy generously over the top.
Serve immediately.

title: Old-Fashioned Potato Candy with Peanut Butter Filling
ingredients: 1/4 cup mashed potato, plain and cooled (no butter or milk added)
3 1/2 to 4 cups powdered sugar, sifted, plus more for rolling
steps: In a large bowl, mix the cooled mashed potato with the salt and vanilla.
Gradually beat in the powdered sugar, about a cup at a time, until a soft, workable dough forms that is no longer sticky.
Turn the dough out onto a surface dusted with powdered sugar and roll into a rectangle about 1/4 inch thick.
Spread the peanut butter evenly over the surface, leaving a small border.
Starting from one long edge, roll the dough up tightly into a log, jelly-roll style.
Wrap the log in plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour, until firm.
Slice the chilled log into 1/4-inch rounds and keep refrigerated until ready to serve.

title: Old-Fashioned Shoofly Pie with Molasses Crumb Topping
steps: Preheat the oven to 375F. Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edges.
In a bowl, combine the flour, brown sugar, and salt; cut in the cold butter with a fork or pastry blender until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Set aside for the topping.
In a separate bowl, whisk the molasses and beaten egg together.
Dissolve the baking soda in the hot water, then whisk it into the molasses mixture; it will foam slightly.
Pour about two-thirds of the molasses mixture into the pie crust.
Sprinkle half of the crumb mixture over the filling, then pour the remaining molasses mixture on top.
Scatter the rest of the crumb topping evenly over the pie.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the crumbs are golden and the center is set but still slightly soft (for a wet-bottom pie) or firmer (bake a few minutes longer for dry-bottom).
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Classic Old-Fashioned Southern Buttermilk Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
steps: Preheat the oven to 350F. Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edges.
In a large bowl, whisk together the sugar and flour.
Add the eggs and whisk until smooth.
Whisk in the melted butter, buttermilk, vanilla, and salt until well combined.
Pour the filling into the unbaked crust and sprinkle the top lightly with nutmeg.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the center is just set with a slight jiggle.
Tent loosely with foil if the top browns too quickly.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate before slicing.

title: Old-Fashioned Chicken and Dumplings Like Grandma Made
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 4 lbs), or 4 bone-in chicken thighs
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
steps: Place the chicken, water, onion, bay leaves, salt, and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, covered, 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until the chicken is very tender and falling off the bone.
Remove the chicken to a plate to cool, then strain the broth and discard the onion and bay leaves. Return the broth to the pot.
Once cool enough to handle, pull the chicken meat from the bones, discarding skin and bones, and shred or chop the meat.
Add the carrots and celery to the broth and simmer 10 minutes, until tender.
For the dumplings, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt, then cut in the butter until crumbly. Stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and bring the broth to a gentle simmer.
Drop the dumpling dough by spoonfuls onto the surface of the simmering broth.
Cover tightly and simmer, without lifting the lid, 15 to 18 minutes, until the dumplings are cooked through and no longer doughy in the center.
Season with additional salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.

title: Old-Fashioned Meatloaf with a Sweet Ketchup Glaze
ingredients: 1 cup breadcrumbs or crushed saltine crackers
steps: Preheat the oven to 350F and lightly grease a loaf pan or line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for a few minutes to soften.
Add the ground beef, chopped onion, eggs, salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and 2 tablespoons of the ketchup.
Mix gently with your hands or a fork just until combined; do not overwork the meat.
Shape the mixture into a loaf and place it in the prepared pan or on the baking sheet.
In a small bowl, stir together the remaining ketchup, brown sugar, and mustard to make the glaze.
Spread the glaze evenly over the top of the loaf.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes, until the meatloaf reaches an internal temperature of 160F.
Let rest 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Old-Fashioned Fried Bologna Sandwich, Depression Style
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Score the edges of each bologna slice in 3-4 places with a sharp knife to keep it from cupping in the skillet.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the bologna slices in batches, 2-3 minutes per side, until the edges curl slightly and the centers are browned and blistered, adding more butter as needed.
If using cheese, lay a slice on top of the bologna during the last 30 seconds of cooking and let it melt.
Meanwhile, spread mustard and mayonnaise on the bread slices.
Stack two slices of fried bologna onto four of the bread slices, season with salt and pepper, and top with the remaining bread.
Serve warm.

title: Old-Fashioned Apple Brown Betty, a Thrifty Classic
ingredients: 4 cups stale bread, torn or cubed (about 6 slices)
4 cups peeled and sliced apples (about 4 medium)
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and butter a 2-quart baking dish.
Toss the bread cubes with the melted butter until evenly coated.
In a separate bowl, toss the sliced apples with lemon juice, half the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Spread one-third of the buttered bread cubes in the bottom of the dish, top with half the apples, and repeat, finishing with a layer of bread cubes on top.
Sprinkle the remaining brown sugar over the top and pour the water or apple juice evenly over the dish.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 15-20 minutes more, until the apples are tender and the top is golden and crisp.
Cool for 10 minutes before serving, plain or with cream or vanilla ice cream.

title: Old-Fashioned Creamy Baked Rice Pudding Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, plus more for dusting
2 tablespoons butter, cut into small pieces
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F and butter a 2-quart baking dish.
In the baking dish, combine the cooked rice, milk, sugar, salt, cinnamon, and raisins, and stir well.
Whisk about 1/2 cup of the warm milk mixture into the beaten eggs to temper them, then stir the eggs back into the dish along with the vanilla.
Dot the top with the butter and dust lightly with additional cinnamon.
Bake uncovered for 60-70 minutes, stirring gently once or twice in the first 30 minutes to prevent a skin from forming too early, until the pudding is set but still slightly jiggly in the center.
Cool for 15 minutes before serving warm, or chill and serve cold.

title: Old-Fashioned Soft Molasses Gingerbread Cake Recipe
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease and flour an 8-inch square baking pan.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves in a bowl.
In a large bowl, cream the lard or butter with the sugar until light, then beat in the egg and molasses.
Add the dry ingredients to the molasses mixture and stir until just combined.
Stir in the boiling water last; the batter will be thin.
Pour into the prepared pan and bake 35-40 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before slicing and serving warm or at room temperature.

title: Old-Fashioned Thrifty Slow-Simmered Beef Stew Recipe
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck roast, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Season the beef with salt and pepper, then toss with 1/4 cup flour to coat.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 3-4 minutes per side; set aside.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes, then add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then return the beef to the pot.
Add the broth, bay leaf, and thyme, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and celery, and continue simmering, covered, for another 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the meat and vegetables are tender.
Mix the remaining 2 tablespoons flour with a little cold water to make a slurry, stir into the stew, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken.
Discard the bay leaf, taste and adjust seasoning, and serve hot with bread.

title: Old-Fashioned Soft Cinnamon-Sugar Snickerdoodles Recipe
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Whisk together the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In a large bowl, cream the butter with 1 1/4 cups of the sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Gradually mix in the dry ingredients until a soft dough forms.
In a small bowl, combine the remaining 1/4 cup sugar with the cinnamon.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and roll each ball in the cinnamon sugar to coat.
Place 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheets and bake 8-10 minutes, until the edges are set but the centers still look slightly soft.
Let cool on the baking sheet for 2 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

title: Old-Fashioned Chess Pie (Just Like Grandma Made)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate, crimping the edges.
Whisk together the sugar, flour, cornmeal, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk in the melted butter, then add the eggs one at a time, whisking well after each.
Whisk in the buttermilk, vinegar, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the filling into the prepared crust.
Bake 45-50 minutes, until the top is golden and cracked and the center still has a slight wobble.
Cool completely on a wire rack, at least 2 hours, before slicing; the filling will finish setting as it cools.

title: Old-Fashioned Tomato Gravy and Biscuits
ingredients: 2 tablespoons bacon drippings or butter (for gravy)
2 cups canned crushed or diced tomatoes with juice
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F. Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt for the biscuits, then cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a soft dough forms; pat out on a floured surface to 3/4-inch thickness and cut into rounds.
Bake the biscuits on a sheet pan for 12-15 minutes, until golden; set aside.
For the gravy, melt the bacon drippings or butter in a skillet over medium heat, whisk in the flour, and cook 1-2 minutes to form a light roux.
Whisk in the tomatoes and milk, and simmer, stirring often, for 8-10 minutes until thickened.
Season with sugar, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes if using.
Split the warm biscuits and spoon the tomato gravy generously over top to serve.

title: Old-Fashioned Peanut Butter Cookies
ingredients: 1/2 cup granulated sugar, plus extra for rolling
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Cream the peanut butter, butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar together until light and fluffy.
Beat in the egg and vanilla until smooth.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt, then mix into the peanut butter mixture until a dough forms.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls, then roll each in a little extra sugar.
Place on the baking sheets and flatten each ball in a crosshatch pattern with the tines of a fork.
Bake 9-11 minutes, until the edges are just set and the centers still look slightly underdone.
Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

title: Old-Fashioned Tuna Noodle Casserole
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cook the egg noodles in salted boiling water until just shy of al dente; drain and set aside.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and mushrooms until softened, about 6-8 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and broth, and simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the cheddar cheese until melted, then fold in the tuna, peas, and cooked noodles; season with salt and pepper.
Spread the mixture into the prepared dish and top evenly with the crushed potato chips.
Bake 20-25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.

title: Old-Fashioned Baked Beans (Slow-Oven Recipe)
ingredients: 6 oz salt pork or thick-cut bacon, diced
2 cups reserved bean cooking liquid or water
steps: Soak the beans in water overnight, then drain.
Place the beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil, and simmer 45-60 minutes until just tender but not falling apart; drain, reserving 2 cups of the cooking liquid.
Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a bean pot or Dutch oven, layer the beans with the salt pork or bacon and onion.
Whisk together the molasses, brown sugar, dry mustard, salt, pepper, and reserved cooking liquid, then pour over the beans.
Cover and bake for 5-6 hours, checking occasionally and adding a little water or reserved liquid if the beans look dry, until deeply flavored and tender.
Uncover for the last 30 minutes of baking to let the sauce thicken and caramelize on top.

title: Southern Fried Cabbage with Bacon
ingredients: 1 medium head cabbage, cored and sliced into thin strips
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
steps: Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp; remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the onion to the bacon drippings and cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the cabbage in batches, letting each addition wilt slightly before adding more.

Pour in the chicken broth, season with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes if using, and cook uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes, until the cabbage is soft and any extra liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the apple cider vinegar and cook 1 minute more.
Return the crispy bacon to the skillet, toss to combine, and serve hot.

title: Old-Fashioned Skillet Cornbread
ingredients: 1/4 cup vegetable oil or melted bacon drippings
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and place a 10-inch cast iron skillet in the oven to heat while you mix the batter.
Whisk together the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, eggs, and oil or bacon drippings.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined.
Carefully remove the hot skillet from the oven, add the butter, and swirl to coat the bottom and sides as it melts.
Pour the batter into the hot, buttered skillet; it should sizzle on contact.
Bake 20-25 minutes, until golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let cool in the skillet for a few minutes before slicing into wedges.

title: Chicken Fried Steak with Gravy
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste
Salt and black pepper, to taste (for gravy)
steps: Season the cube steaks with salt and pepper on both sides.
In one shallow dish, combine 1 cup flour with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. In another, whisk together the eggs and buttermilk.
Dredge each steak in the seasoned flour, then dip in the egg mixture, then dredge again in the flour, pressing to adhere a thick crust.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the steaks 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp; drain on a wire rack and reserve 3 tablespoons of the drippings in the skillet.
Whisk the remaining 2 tablespoons flour into the reserved drippings and cook 1-2 minutes, then gradually whisk in the milk.
Simmer, whisking often, until thickened, about 5 minutes, and season with salt and pepper.
Serve the steaks hot, smothered in the cream gravy.

title: Old-Fashioned Applesauce Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking pan or bundt pan.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and salt.
In a large bowl, cream butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in the applesauce.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing just until combined.
Fold in the raisins and walnuts.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake 40-45 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before serving.

title: Southern Fried Apples
ingredients: 6 medium apples (Granny Smith or Honeycrisp), cored and sliced
steps: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced apples and cook, stirring occasionally, about 5 minutes, until they begin to soften.
Sprinkle in brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt; stir to coat the apples evenly.
Add lemon juice and water or cider, then reduce heat to low and simmer 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the apples are tender and the sauce has thickened.
If a thicker sauce is desired, sprinkle in the flour and stir until dissolved, cooking 1-2 minutes more.
Serve warm as a side, breakfast topping, or dessert.

title: Hamburger Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, 15-20 minutes; drain and mash with butter and milk. Season with salt and pepper and keep warm.
Meanwhile, brown ground beef with diced onion in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking up the meat, until no longer pink; drain excess fat.
Sprinkle flour over the beef and stir, cooking 1-2 minutes to remove the raw flour taste.
Gradually whisk in beef broth, then the milk, stirring constantly until smooth.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, 8-10 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the hamburger gravy ladled generously over the mashed potatoes.

title: Old-Fashioned Sweet Potato Pie
ingredients: 2 cups mashed cooked sweet potatoes (about 2 large)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edges.
In a large bowl, beat mashed sweet potatoes with granulated sugar, brown sugar, and melted butter until smooth.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then mix in the evaporated milk and vanilla.
Stir in cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and salt until fully combined.
Pour the filling into the prepared crust and smooth the top.
Bake 50-55 minutes, until the center is just set and a knife inserted comes out mostly clean.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Old-Fashioned Salisbury Steak with Onion Gravy
steps: In a large bowl, combine ground beef, breadcrumbs, egg, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper; mix gently and shape into 5-6 oval patties.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear patties 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned; remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the sliced onions and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally and scraping up the browned bits, until softened and golden, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the onions and stir, cooking 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce until smooth, then bring to a simmer.
Return the patties to the skillet, cover, and simmer 10-12 minutes until cooked through and the gravy has thickened.
Serve hot, spooning the onion gravy generously over the patties.

title: Old-Fashioned Chicken Pot Pie
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Fit one pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat; add onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk until smooth.
Simmer, stirring constantly, 5-7 minutes until thickened.
Stir in chicken, mixed vegetables, potato, salt, and pepper; remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Pour filling into the prepared crust and top with the second crust, sealing and crimping the edges. Cut a few slits in the top and brush with egg wash.
Bake 35-40 minutes, until the crust is golden brown, tenting with foil if browning too quickly.
Let rest 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Beef and Noodles over Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 2 lbs chuck roast, cut into large chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled, cubed, and mashed with butter and milk
steps: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear beef on all sides until deeply browned, working in batches if needed.
Add onion and garlic to the pot and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Return beef to the pot; add beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf and shred the beef with two forks.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer 2-3 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Cook egg noodles separately according to package directions; drain and fold into the beef and gravy.
Serve the beef and noodles ladled over a bed of mashed potatoes.

title: Split Pea Soup with Ham
ingredients: 1 lb dried split peas, rinsed and picked over
1 meaty ham bone or ham hock
Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 cups diced cooked ham (optional, for extra ham)
steps: Combine split peas, ham bone, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, water or broth, bay leaf, and thyme in a large stockpot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the peas have broken down and the soup is thick and creamy.
Remove the ham bone, let it cool slightly, then pull off any meat and return it to the pot; discard the bone and bay leaf.
Stir in diced ham if using, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
If the soup is thicker than desired, thin with a splash of water or broth.
Ladle hot into bowls and serve with crusty bread.

title: Old-Fashioned Scalloped Potatoes (Just Like Grandma Made)
ingredients: 3 lbs Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat; add onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in milk until smooth.
Cook, whisking constantly, until the sauce thickens, 5-7 minutes; stir in nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Layer half the sliced potatoes in the baking dish, pour over half the sauce, and sprinkle with half the cheese; repeat with remaining potatoes, sauce, and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes, then uncover and bake 25-30 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden and bubbly.
Let rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Old-Fashioned Pineapple Upside-Down Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Melt 1/4 cup butter in a 9-inch cast iron skillet over low heat; sprinkle brown sugar evenly over the melted butter.
Arrange pineapple rings over the brown sugar and place a cherry in the center of each ring.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
In a separate large bowl, cream the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy; beat in eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Alternate adding the flour mixture and milk to the butter mixture, mixing just until combined.
Pour the batter evenly over the pineapple in the skillet, spreading to the edges.
Bake 35-40 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let the cake cool in the skillet 10 minutes, then invert onto a serving platter while still warm.

title: Old-Fashioned Pound Cake Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened, room temperature
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F. Grease and flour a 10-inch tube or bundt pan.
Cream butter and sugar together on medium speed for 5-7 minutes, until very light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Whisk together flour, salt, and baking powder in a separate bowl.
Alternate adding the flour mixture and milk to the butter mixture, beginning and ending with the flour, mixing just until combined.
Stir in the vanilla extract.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake 70-80 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, avoiding opening the oven during the first hour.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Old-Fashioned Chicken and Rice Casserole
ingredients: 1 (10.5 oz) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (10.5 oz) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
In a bowl, whisk together the condensed soups, chicken broth, onion, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Spread the uncooked rice evenly in the bottom of the baking dish.
Pour the soup mixture over the rice and stir to combine.
Place the chicken breasts on top of the rice mixture and season with additional salt and pepper.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 55-65 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F internal temperature.
If using, sprinkle cheese over the top and bake uncovered an additional 5-10 minutes, until melted.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

title: Southern Hush Puppies Recipe
steps: Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a heavy pot or Dutch oven to 350°F.
Whisk together cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the egg, buttermilk, and grated onion.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; the batter will be thick.
Drop the batter by tablespoonfuls into the hot oil, frying in batches so as not to crowd the pot.
Fry 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels or a wire rack.
Serve hot.

title: Old-Fashioned Shepherd's Pie (Cottage Pie)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs ground beef (or ground lamb for traditional shepherd's pie)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, 15-20 minutes; drain and mash with butter and milk, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, brown ground beef in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat, breaking it up as it cooks; drain excess fat.
Add onion, carrots, and garlic; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle in flour and stir to coat, cooking 1 minute.
Stir in beef broth, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce; simmer 5-7 minutes until thickened.
Stir in peas and season with salt and pepper.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the meat filling, running a fork across the top to create ridges.
Bake 25-30 minutes, until the potatoes are golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
